info.description:
**Data360 API** – Contrat d'erreurs : **3 types seulement** (Swagger lisible).

1. **500 – Server down.** Backend ou exception non gérée.
2. **400 / 404 – Snowflake non connecté.** Connexion refusée, session expirée, auth.
3. **422 – Erreur Snowflake (requête SQL).** Format exact comme dans les WARNING, ex. : `000904 (42000): <query_id>: SQL compilation error: error line 2 at position 21`. Réponse avec `detail` et `snowflake: { errno, sqlstate, msg }`.

**Pre-hook (routes protégées) :** POST /signin (body: account_name, username, password) → header `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Sur 401, rappeler POST /signin.

**Hooks par route :** Pre-hook, Post-hook et Inputs (paramètres issus d'autres endpoints) sont documentés dans chaque opération.

Datalake : tag « Datalake Management » et docs/API_DATALAKE_CONNECT_FLOW.md.

Get the current user's allowed modules.

Use this endpoint to refresh user permissions after grants are updated,

get.description:
Dispatch by scope so the hot (default) account-wide list is account-shared
while the per-caller list stays per-user:

  * mine_only=true  → list_projects(username=…) filters rows to the caller's
    owned/contributed projects → PER-USER cache (@session_cache). Sharing it
    would leak one user's project set to another.
  * mine_only=false → list_projects(username=None): no per-user filter, no
    per-user field — every caller in the account gets the identical row set.
    Served from an account-global @shared_cache(query_based) entry
    (shared_query:{account}:_list_projects_shared:{hash}) so the first warm
    load kills the repeated Snowflake read for everyone. This is the default
    and the hot workflow/explore page-load path.

get.description:
Returns projects grouped by type with last activity, contributors,
and cross-module last-used information.

Scope mirrors GET /projects: mine_only=true (default) returns only the
caller's owned/contributed projects; mine_only=false returns all active
account projects (used by the BI landing to list every project).

Dispatch mirrors GET /projects: the mine_only path is per-caller (rows
filtered by username AND a per-user `last_used` map) → PER-USER cache; the
mine_only=false path is account-global (no per-user rows, and `last_used` is
suppressed by get_unified_project_list — see services.py) → account-shared
@shared_cache(query_based).

get.description:
Per-dashboard query cost (credits / bytes scanned) for "expensive chart" detection.

HONEST-PARTIAL: the intended source is Snowflake
``SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY`` (BYTES_SCANNED, CREDITS_USED_*),
mirroring the observability cost endpoints. But a dashboard's render queries
(``POST /bi-dashboard/{id}/render`` → ``build_and_execute_chart``) run on the
shared ``COMPUTE_WH`` warehouse **without a per-dashboard QUERY_TAG**. There is
therefore no attribute on QUERY_HISTORY that ties a query row back to this
specific dashboard.

Correlating by warehouse + time window on a shared warehouse would yield numbers
that look real but are not actually attributable to this dashboard — a fake
number under the project rule. So we DO NOT invent a cost: we return the
dashboard identity with ``partial: true``, ``cost: null``, and a note describing
the concrete fix (tag render queries so future QUERY_HISTORY rows are
attributable). A bogus ``dashboard_id`` still 404s, matching the other
per-dashboard routes.

post.summary: Refresh a stale data product's backing object (ALTER DYNAMIC TABLE … REFRESH)
post.description:
Refresh the materialization behind a data product.

A data product is metadata over an existing ``TABLE_FQN`` — there is no
stored "defining query" to re-run (unlike a project transform). The backing
object is refreshed in place:

  • Dynamic table → ``ALTER DYNAMIC TABLE <fqn> REFRESH`` (synchronous
    manual refresh; the only object kind with a manual refresh verb).
  • Materialized view → auto-maintained by Snowflake; no manual refresh.
  • Plain table → no refresh semantics (data is already at rest).
  • View → always live; nothing to refresh.

We attempt the dynamic-table refresh and, when the backing object is not a
dynamic table, return an honest ``refreshed: false`` with the reason rather
than a fake success. ``LAST_REFRESHED_AT`` is stamped on a successful
refresh so the marketplace freshness badge updates.

post.summary: Validate connector connectivity config (no fake success)
post.description:
Config-validation for a connector. The platform cannot truly reach every
external system generically, so this runs real, honest checks:

  1. required params (from the catalog entry) present in the request body
  2. if a `storage_integration` is supplied → SHOW INTEGRATIONS LIKE it
  3. if a `stage` is supplied → SHOW STAGES LIKE it

round-trips — each going proxy → NextAuth → backend → Snowflake and issuing FOUR
Snowflake round-trips (``ALTER SESSION``=10, ``SHOW GRANTS``, fetch, ``ALTER
SESSION``=60). With ~20-40 account roles that aggregate reached ~38s cold. Here the
N ``SHOW GRANTS`` run back-to-back on the single persistent service connection
(no per-call proxy/auth overhead, statement-timeout set ONCE) under one wall-clock
budget, then cached account-global like the per-role drill — so a cold call is a
handful of seconds and a warm call is a cache hit.

Returns ``{ grants: { <role>: [grant-row, …] }, partial, skipped_roles, note }`` —
the grant rows keep the exact ``SHOW GRANTS`` shape the FE already normalises, so
the FE keeps its ``grantsMap`` aggregation untouched. Degrades HONESTLY: when the
wall-clock budget is spent the remaining roles are listed in ``skipped_roles`` with
``partial: true`` so the FE renders "—"/warming for them rather than a fabricated
complete grid (no fake zeros).

get.summary: Top API endpoints by request count
get.description:
Aggregate EVENT_STORE.AUDIT_LOG: top endpoints by request count.

Groups by METHOD + ACTION (request path) and carries MODULE.
`errors` counts rows with STATUS_CODE >= 400.

get.summary: AUDIT_LOG request counts grouped by a dimension
get.description:
Group EVENT_STORE.AUDIT_LOG requests by module, D360 role, or user.

`dimension` selects a SQL column — it is resolved through a fixed whitelist
(never interpolated raw) before being placed in the query.

Aggregate EVENT_STORE.USER_ACTIVITY events by module, project, and user.

`failures` follows the repo convention (STATUS = 'ERROR'), matching
observability/services.py module-summary aggregation.

USER_ACTIVITY is per-account: the read MUST run on the requesting user's
account (mirrors command_center.route_activity_feed → get_read_connection),
NOT the fixed admin events account, otherwise the table is empty/inaccessible.

Live ops-dashboard snapshot from in-memory request metrics.

Source: ``app.core.metrics_middleware`` (RequestMetricsMiddleware records
EVERY request, GET included). This is IN-MEMORY and NOT Snowflake-backed,
so the numbers are **per-worker** — with uvicorn ``--workers N`` each worker
has its own counters and this reflects whichever worker served the request.

Returns: requests/min + /5min, totals, error rate, uptime, memory/cpu,
latency percentiles, top + slowest endpoints, recent 4xx/5xx errors, and
active users by request volume.

get.summary: Snowflake query + related events behind a probed api-health call
get.description:
Resolve a Snowflake ``query_id`` to its QUERY_HISTORY row + related events.

ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY first (durable, ~45 min–3 h latency), falling
back to ``TABLE(INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY())`` (recent, low-latency)
when the durable view has no row yet — the common case for a just-probed
call. Related HTTP events come from EVENT_STORE.USER_REQUESTS, correlated by
the query's time window, and degrade to ``[]`` if the spine is empty/absent
(no SVC locally). Every numeric field is real or ``null`` (no fake 0).

get.summary: Cache warm coverage per account/role + @shared_cache self-check
get.description:
Cache coverage: live (account, role) tuples from the event store, per-account
SVC presence, and the warmer's @shared_cache command-center coverage self-check
(declared vs. covered vs. cold-every-TTL routes).

Read-only. Active-role discovery uses the background SVC connection (returns []
when no SVC/event store yet → degrades to "account-global only"). Never 500s.

get.summary: Per-account SVC connection health (+ dev-fallback flag)
get.description:
Per-account service-account connection state, with the dev-fallback flag.

Reuses the svc-registry probe (alive / auth_type per ``_svc_configs`` entry) and
adds ``fallback_enabled`` — when True on a prod box, reads can silently fall back
to the user connection instead of failing closed (an operator should see this).
Also reports the global background/admin connection availability + the live
in-flight service-query count. Read-only; never 500s.

post.summary: Trigger a one-account cache warm pass
post.description:
Run ONE warm pass for a single account on demand.

Warms every account-global @shared_cache target (+ per-project targets) via the
warmer's validated path. With ``per_role=true`` AND CACHE_WARM_PER_ROLE enabled,
also warms role-dependent surfaces once per active role; with ``per_role=true``
but the flag OFF, the per-role step reports ``skipped: disabled`` (the manual
trigger does NOT bypass the env gate — per-role warm is a deliberate opt-in,
pending the connection-routing fix). Returns the warm summary; never 500s.

post.summary: Precisely evict one UI surface for one account (all roles)
post.description:
Evict exactly one UI surface for one account (all roles) + its shared slots.

Delegates to intelligent_cache.invalidate_ui_surface — account-scoped (never
``d360:*``), key patterns derived from the same builders the @account_role_cache
decorator uses (zero drift). ``dry_run=true`` previews the patterns without
touching Redis. Never 500s (invalidate_ui_surface never raises).
